name: issue_827_away_setback_floor_breach
description: Issue #827 GAP-6 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). While the home is away, the same nearest-edge selector runs against the SETBACK band [setback_heat 60F, setback_cool 80F]. Indoor decays from 72F through 65F (inside the setback band's interior, mode kept) to 57F, 3F below the setback floor, and the first away evaluation below the floor (08:30) arms heat at the setback floor (60F), not at comfort_heat (68F). This is a deliberate Design D behavior change: before #1066 an empty house below its setback floor stayed in cool at the setback ceiling.
source: Issue #827 Design table, GAP-6 -- away/vacation uses the same mechanism, different bounds, not a separate code path.
notes: Occupant impact: an empty house must not freeze (pipes, belongings) while the household is away, and must not be heated to the comfort temperature either. Heat is armed at the setback floor (60F) so energy use stays minimal.

Design D rule exercised (docs/08 section 6f): indoor < floor -> heating immediately; the band is the setback band while away. The 08:32 re-tick is a redundant re-affirmation kept from the original timeline; final-state assertions cannot prove WHEN heating was armed. The 08:30 expect_band(ceiling 80) assertion reads only band edges (which are 60/80 regardless of the armed family), so it is a weak check that the setback band, not the comfort band, is in force; it no longer proves 'no premature escalation'.

Baseline fix (Issue #1066 review): the original baseline sat inside the heat zone (indoor <= floor + m), so heat was already armed before the breach and the final-state assertions passed vacuously. The baseline is now inside the cooling zone so the breach reading is the first thing that can arm heat. (The original 65F baseline was below the 68F comfort floor, so heat was armed at 08:00 at home, before the away transition.)

occupancy_away is dispatched as a direct event both to enter away mode and to re-tick the setback evaluation after indoor decays, mirroring production's per-cycle re-affirmation of the away setback band (apply_classification() DEFER_OCCUPANCY path).
day_type is 'warm' (hvac_mode=off, as classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_WARM) only as a plausible daytime context; the away/vacation band selection does not depend on the day type.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: if _apply_occupancy_away_vacation_decision() bypassed _apply_comfort_band() (calling _set_temperature() directly), comfort_family and expect_band(floor 60) would fail. With nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main) away mode always resolves the ceiling as the active edge (cooling base family); heat is against-grain, needing the warm deadband, recency and a 90 s sustain across two evaluations, so the empty house stays in cool below the setback floor and comfort_family=heating / last_hvac_mode=heat fail.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('Away/vacation, empty house below the setback floor: cool at the setback ceiling before, heat now (behavior change)').

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: an empty house keeps drifting colder than the setback floor with no heat (freeze risk), or is heated to the full comfort temperature while nobody is home.

events.note: Baseline classification while still home (warm day, classifier hvac_mode=off).

Indoor 72F, inside the normal comfort band [68F, 74F] (cooling zone, >= 74 - 2): cool is armed while home. (The original 65F baseline was below the 68F floor, which armed heat before the household even left.)

Occupant leaves. handle_occupancy_away() applies the setback band via select_comfort_band(occupancy_mode=away): floor=setback_heat(60), ceiling=setback_cool(80), active='ceiling' -> base_family='cooling'. Indoor(65) > 60, no breach.

Indoor 65F: below the comfort floor (68F) but inside the away setback band [60F, 80F], strictly between 62F and 78F (floor + m, ceiling - m): the thermostat keeps its current mode (cool at the setback ceiling). The comfort floor no longer applies while away.

Re-tick (mirrors apply_classification()'s per-cycle DEFER_OCCUPANCY re-affirmation while still away). Indoor 57F is below the setback floor (60F): floor breach, heat is armed at the setback floor immediately.
Re-tick 2 minutes later: still below the setback floor, heating remains armed (redundant re-affirmation kept from the original timeline).

assertions.reason: Baseline: away-mode setback band [60F, 80F] armed on entry, matching setback_heat/setback_cool, not the daytime comfort band.

The setback band edges (ceiling 80F) are still the ones in force at the first below-floor tick. Band-edge check only: the band is [60F, 80F] regardless of which family is armed, so this does not by itself prove the family; the family and mode are asserted at 08:32:00.
GAP-6 fix: the away-mode setback floor gets the same nearest-edge defense as the occupied comfort floor; a breach arms heating (final-state assertion; armed at the first below-floor tick, 08:30).
The commanded heat target is the SETBACK floor (60F), not comfort_heat (68F), proving the away-mode arm defends the correct (setback) floor.
The commanded mode is a real climate service call, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: While away, indoor below the setback floor arms heat at the setback floor (60F) on the first evaluation.
verdict.observed_behavior: Away band [60F, 80F] armed on entry; the 57F reading at 08:30 arms heating, and heat is commanded at the setback floor, not at comfort_heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: The nearest-edge selector uses the setback band while away; an empty house below its setback floor gets heat at the setback floor (docs/08 section 6f).
